metaTitle: Kitchen Remodeling Contractors in Ontario: A Guide
metaDescription: What to know before hiring a kitchen remodeler in Ontario, including RTA versus custom cabinetry, trade sequencing, realistic costs and red flags.
intro: A kitchen remodel touches cabinetry, countertops, electrical and plumbing all at once, which makes sequencing and trade coordination as important as the finishes you choose. Deciding between ready-to-assemble and custom cabinetry early shapes both budget and timeline.
whatToLookFor: Clear explanation of RTA versus custom or semi-custom cabinetry
A sequencing plan for electrical and plumbing rough-in before cabinets go in
Accurate measuring and a detailed layout drawing before ordering materials
Countertop templating done after cabinets are installed, not before
A realistic timeline that accounts for lead times on custom orders
typicalCostNotes: Kitchen remodel costs can range from a modest cabinet and countertop refresh to a full gut renovation with layout changes, and the spread often comes down to cabinetry choice, countertop material and whether plumbing or electrical is relocated. RTA cabinetry generally costs less than custom work, though lead times can sometimes offset the savings, and layout changes that move plumbing or electrical will add to both cost and schedule. Get a written breakdown by category so cabinetry, counters and labour are each visible.
questionsToAsk: Are we using RTA, semi-custom or fully custom cabinetry, and why?
How do you sequence electrical and plumbing rough-in with the cabinet install?
When is the countertop template taken, and what is the lead time?
What happens if we change our layout after ordering starts?
Who is responsible for coordinating the electrician and plumber?
redFlags: Countertops measured before cabinets are actually installed
No clarity on cabinet type or where it is manufactured
Rough-in trades booked with no coordination plan
